sentences.text:
For the Resp. No.2 : Mr. Perwej Ahmad, Advocate -----------
th 04/Dated: 06 August, 2025 I.A. No.1333 of 2025 This Criminal Appeal has been filed on behalf of the appellant challenging the judgment of conviction dated 07.01.2025 and sentence dated 10.01.2025 passed in POCSO Case No.29 of 2024, arising out of Mirzachouki P.S. Case No.24 of 2024 by Sri Birendra Kumar Srivastava, learned Special Judge POCSO Act, Sahibganj by which the appellant has been convicted for the offences under section 376(3)/511 of IPC, section 10 of the POCSO Act and under section 3(1) of the SC/ST Act and sentenced to undergo R.I. for seven (07)
years and to pay fine of Rs.25,000/- for the offence under section 10 of the POCSO Act and further sentenced to undergo R.I for five (05) years and to pay the fine of Rs.10,000/ for the offence under section 3(1) of the SC/ST Act.
However, all the sentences have been directed to run concurrently.
2. I.A. No.1333 of 2025 has been filed on behalf of the appellant for suspension of sentence and for grant of bail to the appellant, during pendency of the present Criminal Appeal.
3. Heard Gautam Kumar, learned counsel for the appellant, Mr. Sardhu Mahto, learned APP for the State and Mr. Perwej Ahmad, learned counsel for the Informant-Respondent No.2 4.
Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that judgment and sentence passed by the learned Trial Court is illegal and not sustainable in law.

It has been submitted that the appellant has been Rustam Ansari @ Md. Rustam Ansari vs State Of Jharkhand on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141424702/
1 falsely implicated by the informant due to village politics and also in view of the fact that appellant had demanded certain money in lieu of goat which had died and even for ousting to the informant.

sentences.text: It has
been submitted that although P.W-1 has not given her statement, however, the medical report of P.W-1 i.e. Victim girl does not support the prosecution case regarding rape.
It is submitted that no case under section 10 of POCSO Act made out as there is no sign of sexual assault and no bodily injury has been found by the doctor.

It is submitted that the appellant is in custody since 28.02.2024 and hence the appellant may be enlarged on bail.
5.

On the other hand, learned APP has opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that the Victim girl is a physically and mentally challenged girl aged around 15 years and she had been subjected to sexual assault and hence there is no illegality in the impugned judgment and sentence passed by the learned Trial Court below.
6. Learned counsel for the informant, after adopting the submission of learned APP, has submitted that the Victim girl is a mentally challenged girl and she was unable to speak.
It is submitted that taking advantage of physical and mental condition the appellant had taken advantage and had sexually assaulted her and hence the prayer for bail of the appellant may be rejected.

7. Perused the Trial Court Record and considered the submission of both the sides.
8.

It reveals from the FIR that on 28.02.2024 while the informant returned to his house at around 4.00 p.m. then he found that the appellant was sleeping beside his daughter and cloth of her daughter was totally opened and then the appellant fled away.
Thereafter, he called his wife and his wife put clothes upon her daughter.
9. From perusal of the statement of informant and his wife i.e. P.W-1 and P.W-2, it reveals that they have supported the allegation made in the FIR and has supported the prosecution case.

10. It further reveals from the Trial Court Record that the learned Trial Court has mentioned the name of Victim girl as well as her father and mother which should have avoided in the light of the judgment reported in (2019) 2 SCC 703 (Nipun Saxena and Anr. vs. Union of India & Ors.).
11.

sentences.text:
It appears from the Trial Court judgment that FSL report of DNA extract of the semen positive pajama cuttings and semen positive hairs cutting of the victim and semen positive underwear,
trouser and, body warmer cuttings and semen positive cotton bud cuttings of pubic area swab of the accused is matched with the accused appellant as paragraph-03, 11, 12, 13 of the report and para-01 to 05 of the conclusion of the FSL report.
Thereafter the Trial Court has convicted the appellant for the offences as mentioned earlier.

12. It further appears that the P.W-2 and P.W-3 who are the father and mother of the Victim girl have supported the allegation against the appellant and P.W-2 had seen him in his house when he returned to his house and found his daughter in naked condition.

He had handed over the entire cloth of his daughter to the police though the same was not produced during trial and for which, the appellant tried to take contradiction and the same has been indicated by the Trial Court that these Rustam Ansari @ Md. Rustam Ansari vs State Of Jharkhand on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141424702/
2 are the manner/activities cannot be seen in the case of physically and mentally challenged girl.

entities.text: Rustam Ansari @ Md. Rustam Ansari vs State Of Jharkhand on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even P.W-2 during his cross examination has denied any financial relation with the goat grazing etc. with the appellant.
13. It reveals that the appellant and the informant are known to each other and the appellant has taken advantage of the mental and physical condition of the Victim girl.
14. P.W-4 is the I.O of this case and who has stated that Victim girl is a mentally challenged and has submitted charge sheet against the appellant.
15. From perusal of the FSL report of the DNA extract, it would appear that the swab of the Victim is matched with the accused-appellant.
16. In view of the above, this Court is not inclined to enlarge the appellant on bail.
17. Accordingly, the I.A. No.1333 of 2025 is, hereby, rejected.

(Sanjay Prasad, J.) Saket/-
